title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system. Version 0.5: Razar reads 20 MB of Spanish Wikipedia in 400 s instead of version 0.3's 1,873 s (82% fewer instructions), and the 15 MB Spanish Wiktionary in 106 s instead of 194 s. It learns exactly the same thing: the MATS result is identical (451 to 117; 249 to 41), and the deduced relations, what it imagined, the pending hypotheses, the mechanisms and the witnesses are byte-identical to version 0.3's. The gain grows with the size of the book, because what was removed (rewriting its notebook whole on every piece) grew with it. The author's Venn becomes part of Janax's architecture: a kernel engine that knows no boxes or files. It takes two sets through a five-question port and a Venn word, with one field per axis (regions, which side is looked at first, a criterion, direction, scope, how many), and gives the selection in order; a bit with no axis yet is refused, so a new axis never changes an old program. The association request (a child born with part of two processes' capabilities) is its first user, tested on the three kernel engines. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar, un razonamiento artificial. v0.5: 20 MB de Wikipedia en 400 s, lo mismo aprendido, y el Venn del autor en la arquitectura. Prototipo de investigación.
